infoText.about: Showing up is the goal. After 50, consistency is more important than sets or reps. Keep moving, stay injury-free, feel good doing it.
infoText.setsAndReps: I usually do 3 sets with a 1/2 weight add-on finisher. Somewhere between 10 and 15 reps where the last few feel like work but form never breaks. Rest usually 2 minutes per set.
infoText.floor: Three movements per session. Primary option first, alternative after the slash — use whichever is free. No supersets, no circuits. Do your sets, rest, move on.
infoText.burnout: Optional. Drop your main compound to 50–60% of working weight and take it to failure. Aim for 20–30 reps. Maintains muscle without heavy loading.
infoText.mat: Over time you should develop your own stretch and core routine using the suggestions here. What we suggest here augments what you already know. The hamstring stretch is a daily constant. Everything else rotates. Props are always optional.
infoText.whenToGo: No streaks. No guilt. The app picks up exactly where you left off — tomorrow or next week, it does not matter.

rules.moveOn: Hit the target with clean form 2 sessions in a row.
rules.regress: Pain, a giving-out feeling, form breaking down, or can't reach the bottom of the range. Also regress if you have to arch your back to reach the position.

phases.name: Phase 1: Training Program
phases.goal: Rotate 1A → 2A → 3A → 4A → 1B → 2B → 3B → 4B. Each exercise moves up its own ladder at its own pace.
warmup: Wrist rocks on all fours: 10 fingers forward, 10 back
Band external rotations, light band: 2 x 15 each arm
Wrist push-ups (rock up onto fingers): 2 x 10
Right shoulder: lying dowel overhead reach, ribs down: 10

2A: Pull · Mat → Machines · BRING: MAT, DUMBBELLS, KETTLEBELL, RACK BAR, PULLDOWN MACHINE, ASSISTED PULL-UP/DIP MACHINE
2B: Pull · Mat → Bench → Machines · BRING: MAT, BAND, DUMBBELLS, BENCH, RACK BAR, CABLE
3A: Skill & Core · Mat · BRING: MAT, WALL, FOAM ROLLER, DOWEL, BENCH, LOW BAR
3B: Skill & Core · Mat · BRING: MAT, WALL, BAND, FOAM ROLLER, DOWEL, BENCH

4B: Legs & Glutes · Mat → Bench → Machines · BRING: MAT, WALL, DUMBBELLS, LEG PRESS, ABDUCTOR MACHINE

Legs straighten as flexibility improves. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

ladders.cueFull: Hold first, then the single-arm work in the same set. On the wall: back your feet up and place your toes at the mark, press toes into the wall, hands stay planted. Shift weight slowly, grip the floor, stop before the shoulder gives. Wall marks at 1, 2 and 3 ft (tape or wall features). Roller step: press it with a foot first to check it's wedged before putting weight on it. Have a medicine ball? Rolling it under one hand works for the fingertip-hover step too.

Tight hamstrings: bend your knees a little so your back stays flat. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

Tight hamstrings: bend your knees a little so your back stays flat and arms stay in line with your ears. Legs straighten as flexibility improves. Ribs down: if your back arches to get your arms overhead, bring your hands forward. Your right shoulder has less range; don't force it.

phases.graduation: Reach the top of every ladder to unlock the forearm headstand phase.
extraChecks: Wrist rocks: 20 reps, pain-free the next day
One full week with no shoulder pain or slipping feeling

One full week with no shoulder pain or slipping feeling
Wall test: right thumb touches the wall overhead with back and ribs flat (needed before chest-to-wall work)
4 weeks of left shoulder work with no instability or giving-out episodes

phases.name: Phase 2: Forearm Headstand
phases.goal: Main goal: forearm headstand at the wall, then a few seconds away from it with a practiced, controlled exit. Plus full L-sit and strict pull-ups.

phases.name: Phase 3: Wall Handstand (optional)
phases.goal: Only if the right-shoulder wall test passes and the left shoulder has been solid for months: wall walks, chest-to-wall holds, wall shoulder taps. No kick-ups or freestanding work.
